Retry-After.description: Seconds before retrying. Sent only with a 503 that clears on its own: `control_plane_overloaded`, when no database connection came free, and a billing action refused while another holds the account's customer or every billing place.

Error.description: OpenAI-shaped error; raw upstream bodies are never returned

RateLimited.description: Entitlement or GPU admission capacity limit

Access-Control-Expose-Headers.description: Response headers a browser client may read

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, or unknown Cloud key

AccessControlExposeHeaders.description: The response headers a browser client may read, as a comma-separated list; it names x-request-id, Retry-After and Server-Timing when the response carries them.

ApiError.description: One closed error shape for every non-public control-plane route.
ApiError.title: ApiError

CancelRequestResponse.description:
Answer to a cancel that reached an in-flight request the caller owns.

`status` is "cancelling", not "cancelled": the node has ended the request's
context and told the engine to abort; the stream's own end and its
settlement follow a moment later on their own path.
CancelRequestResponse.title: CancelRequestResponse

CatalogModelResponse.description:
One entitled model, priced. Straight from `pricing.catalog()` - the same
numbers the credit gate charges against, so a published price cannot drift
from a billed one (G7).
CatalogModelResponse.title: CatalogModelResponse

CliUsageEvent.description:
One request, as the CLI shows it.

A narrower projection than the console's: no prompt text, and none of the
max-token accounting a terminal has no use for.
CliUsageEvent.title: CliUsageEvent

CliUsageWindow.description:
Spend over a window ending now, not a calendar bucket.

`timeline` cannot answer this. It groups by `usage_date`, so its finest
grain is a whole day and its most recent point is "today so far", which
drifts from an hour to a day depending on what time it is read. It also
carries no `cached_tokens`. `UsageTotals` carries all four numbers a
terminal shows, so a window is a totals query with a different `since`.

`seconds` is the span, carried so a client never has to parse `window`.
CliUsageWindow.title: CliUsageWindow

CliUsageWindowLabel.description:
The two windows `rcli usage` draws. Closed, because the endpoint offers
no way to ask for a third: a client can switch on these and be exhaustive.
CliUsageWindowLabel.title: CliUsageWindowLabel

OpenRouterFeature.description: One request feature, as OpenRouter names it (for example tools, reasoning). Informational: a plain string, never an enum, so a value added later cannot fail a client's parser; the vocabulary is enforced where the value is generated (scripts/generate_constants.py).

OpenRouterInputModality.description: One input modality, as OpenRouter names it (for example text, image). Informational: a plain string, never an enum, so a value added later cannot fail a client's parser; the vocabulary is enforced where the value is generated (scripts/generate_constants.py).

OpenRouterOutputModality.description: One output modality, as OpenRouter names it (for example text). Informational: a plain string, never an enum, so a value added later cannot fail a client's parser; the vocabulary is enforced where the value is generated (scripts/generate_constants.py).

OpenRouterPricing.description: USD per ONE token, as decimal strings so no float rounds them. OpenRouter's legacy provider field (openrouter.ai/docs 'Provider Integration (Legacy Format)'), added by the gateway to an entry whose model is described to OpenRouter; OpenAI clients ignore it.

OpenRouterQuantization.description: A weight precision, as OpenRouter names it (for example fp8, nvfp4). Informational: a plain string, never an enum, so a value added later cannot fail a client's parser; the vocabulary is enforced where the value is generated (scripts/generate_constants.py).

OpenRouterSamplingParameter.description: One sampling parameter, as OpenRouter names it (for example temperature, top_p). Informational: a plain string, never an enum, so a value added later cannot fail a client's parser; the vocabulary is enforced where the value is generated (scripts/generate_constants.py).

context_length.description: The whole context window in tokens, prompt and output together -- not max_input_tokens, which is the largest prompt this deployment still answers. OpenRouter's legacy provider field (openrouter.ai/docs 'Provider Integration (Legacy Format)'), added by the gateway to an entry whose model is described to OpenRouter; OpenAI clients ignore it.

created.description: OpenAI-shaped creation timestamp (unix seconds) the gateway reports; informational.

hugging_face_id.description: The Hugging Face repository OpenRouter groups this model's providers by (org/repo), or empty when the model is not on Hugging Face. OpenRouter's legacy provider field (openrouter.ai/docs 'Provider Integration (Legacy Format)'), added by the gateway to an entry whose model is described to OpenRouter; OpenAI clients ignore it.

input_modalities.description: What a request may carry. OpenRouter's legacy provider field (openrouter.ai/docs 'Provider Integration (Legacy Format)'), added by the gateway to an entry whose model is described to OpenRouter; OpenAI clients ignore it.

max_input_tokens.description: The advertised ceiling on input tokens for this model -- what an OpenAI-shaped coding agent reads to decide when to compact. It is the largest prompt the engine still answers with one output token, not the raw context length: a prompt longer than this is refused with 400 before it is billed. null means the deployment has not established one.

max_output_length.description: The most output tokens one request can be granted. OpenRouter's legacy provider field (openrouter.ai/docs 'Provider Integration (Legacy Format)'), added by the gateway to an entry whose model is described to OpenRouter; OpenAI clients ignore it.

max_output_tokens.description: The advertised ceiling on output tokens, when the deployment declares one separately from the context window. null means this model draws output from the single budget max_input_tokens already describes.

mode.description: The gateway's model mode; every Wally model is a chat model.

name.description: The model's display name. OpenRouter's legacy provider field (openrouter.ai/docs 'Provider Integration (Legacy Format)'), added by the gateway to an entry whose model is described to OpenRouter; OpenAI clients ignore it.

output_modalities.description: What a response carries. OpenRouter's legacy provider field (openrouter.ai/docs 'Provider Integration (Legacy Format)'), added by the gateway to an entry whose model is described to OpenRouter; OpenAI clients ignore it.

quantization.description: The served weights' precision, as OpenRouter names it. OpenRouter's legacy provider field (openrouter.ai/docs 'Provider Integration (Legacy Format)'), added by the gateway to an entry whose model is described to OpenRouter; OpenAI clients ignore it.

supported_features.description: The request features this model honours, each measured live; an absent name is unsupported. OpenRouter's legacy provider field (openrouter.ai/docs 'Provider Integration (Legacy Format)'), added by the gateway to an entry whose model is described to OpenRouter; OpenAI clients ignore it.

supported_sampling_parameters.description: The sampling parameters this model honours, each measured live; an absent name is unsupported. OpenRouter's legacy provider field (openrouter.ai/docs 'Provider Integration (Legacy Format)'), added by the gateway to an entry whose model is described to OpenRouter; OpenAI clients ignore it.

ServerTiming.description: W3C Server-Timing. As a HEADER it carries pre-stream phases only, for example the gateway's authorize call and the sidecar's ra-queue (time waiting for a seat) and ra-admit (the sidecar's own work before the request reached the model). Time to first token is never in the header, because it is not known when the headers are sent; on a streaming response it arrives as a Server-Timing TRAILER named ra-ttft, after the last SSE frame. Metric names are not a closed set: ignore a name you do not know, and treat the trailer as optional.

UsageRequestPage.description:
One page of an account's settled request history, newest first.

Every row is a settled usage event: a hold still open, or a request refused
before anything wrote usage for it, is not in this list. `as_of` is the
snapshot the first page took, a minute behind the ledger's clock; every
page of one export (follow
`next_cursor`, sending the same `since`, `until` and filters) reports rows
written at or before it, and `totals` covers all of them. A request that
settles later appears in the next fresh export. `next_cursor` is null on
the last page.
UsageRequestPage.title: UsageRequestPage

UsageRequestRecord.description:
One settled request, as the ledger recorded and charged it.

`cost_micros` is the amount charged: the priced cost, or 0 when the failure
was ours (status >= 500). `noncached_prompt_tokens` is DERIVED, not an
engine count: the prompt less its cached subset, clamped the way pricing
clamps it, so it is the fresh input `cost_micros` was priced on.
`reasoning_tokens` is reported as the engine sent it and is not guaranteed
to be a subset of `completion_tokens`. `request_id` is the ledger's own,
unique id; `response_request_id` is the `x-request-id` the response carried,
which is what a client logs, and is null when none was recorded.
`ts_start`/`ts_end` are when the request ran; `recorded_at` is when the
ledger wrote the row. No prompt or completion text, key material or account
identity is ever included.
UsageRequestRecord.title: UsageRequestRecord

UsageRequestTotals.description: The whole snapshot's totals, identical on every page of one export.
UsageRequestTotals.title: UsageRequestTotals

UsdPerToken.description: A non-negative USD amount per token as a plain decimal string: never exponent form, no trailing zeros.

info.description: CLI-facing operations extracted from control-plane-v1.openapi.json by contracts/extract-cli-contract.py. Do not hand-edit.
info.title: Wally CLI control-plane contract (extract)

post.description:
Invalidate both halves of an RCLI login.

The response is always 204, including for an unknown or already-revoked
credential. Logout is safe to retry after a lost response, and callers do
not get a token-validity oracle.

Open an authorization request. Unauthenticated by design: the terminal
has no credential yet, which is the reason this flow exists.

Being unauthenticated is also why it is rate limited. Nothing here costs a
customer anything, but a row is written per call and the endpoint is public.

get.description:
One read: the balance, the window's totals, and how they were spent.

A terminal draws its whole report in one go, so splitting this across three
round-trips would only give the CLI three chances to render a report whose
parts disagree about when they were taken.

The account's settled requests in `[since, until)`, newest first.

Both ends must carry a timezone and span at most 31 days. To read the next
page, send the same window and filters with `cursor` set to the previous
page's `next_cursor`; a cursor from a different window, filter set or
account is refused rather than reinterpreted. `api_key_id` and
`request_id` narrow within this account only, so another account's key or
request reads as an empty page, never as a 404.

`response_request_id` finds the rows for the `x-request-id` a response
carried -- the id a client logs; `request_id` is the ledger's own. The
former is a label rather than a key, so it may match more than one row.

`rcli whoami`. Authenticated by the API key the CLI was issued, because
that is the only credential it has.

The contract declares that key as `BearerAuth`. The same Authorization
header also carries the console's signed PropelAuth session token, and
where PropelAuth is not configured, never in production, the `X-User-Id`
and `X-User-Email` development identity headers are accepted instead.
Neither is a separate security scheme: this contract declares no console
session scheme on any operation, and the development headers are not a
credential.

get.summary: List models available to the current key

get.description:
Which models we serve and what they cost.

The console used to name a single model from a config constant, which was
true when the endpoint served one and became wrong the moment LiteLLM sat in
front of three. Prices come from the same catalog the gate charges against,
so a published price cannot drift from a billed one.

post.description:
End an in-flight request the caller's key started (#440).

`request_id` is the `x-request-id` the customer received on the response
being cancelled. The GPU nodes are asked on this service's behalf with the
credential they already hold for this ledger (see services/cancel.py), and
each ends the request only if that key started it. Anything else -- an id
nobody is serving, a request that already finished, someone else's -- is
the same 404, so this route cannot be used to learn about other customers'
requests. A successful cancel is 202: the node has told the engine to stop;
the stream's end and its settlement follow on their own path.
